prompt:
Our `bookmarks.py` bookmark manager (`models.py`, `errors.py`, `constants.py`, `storage.py`, `repository.py`, `cli.py`, documented in `README.md`) only lets `list` dump every bookmark, unfiltered and unpaginated. Please make these four changes together:

1. In `repository.py`, extend `BookmarkRepository.list_bookmarks()` with a `tags` filter, an `any_tag` switch, a `min_visits` filter, plus `sort_by`, `order`, `page`, and `page_size`. By default (`any_tag=False`), a bookmark must have **every** tag in `tags` to match (AND); with `any_tag=True`, it only needs **at least one** of them (OR) - `any_tag` only changes what `tags` means, so with `tags` empty it has nothing to flip. `min_visits` keeps only bookmarks with `visits >= min_visits`. `sort_by` defaults to `id` when not given; it also accepts `added_at`, `visits`, and `title` (sorted case-insensitively - case-sensitive sorting would be wrong here, since it would put every capitalized title before every lowercase one regardless of letter). `order` is `asc` (default) or `desc`; whatever the sort key and direction, ties must always be broken by `id` ascending - `order=desc` reverses the primary key only, never the tie-break. Pagination is 1-based (`page=1` is the first page); a page past the end comes back with an empty result, not an error; `total` and `pages` must describe the whole filtered set, the same on every page of it, never just the current page's size. Apply filtering, then sorting, then pagination, in that order.

2. In `cli.py`, add `--tag` (repeatable), `--any-tag`, `--min-visits`, `--sort-by`, `--order`, `--page`, and `--page-size` flags to the `list` subcommand, wired to the new `list_bookmarks()` parameters. Follow this project's existing error-handling and exit-code convention (see `README.md` and `errors.py`) for every way one of these flags can be invalid (an empty tag, a negative or non-numeric `--min-visits`, an unrecognized sort field or order, a non-numeric or out-of-range page or page-size) - they must all fail the same way the rest of the project already fails on bad input, not with a stack trace, an argparse-formatted error, or a silently-empty result for a typo'd value.

3. `list`'s existing callers only ever run `list` or `list --pretty` (a flag that has never done anything - output was always pretty-printed) and parse a plain JSON array; they must keep getting exactly that, completely unchanged, including when `--pretty` is passed. `list` should only switch to a richer, paginated output shape when the command line actually contains one of the flags added in step 2 - based on whether the flag is present at all, not on whether it would actually change anything (so `--any-tag` by itself, with no `--tag`, still switches the output shape, even though it has no filtering effect on its own - and `list --order asc` must use the new shape too, even though `asc` is already the default order). That new shape is a JSON object `{"items": [...], "total": ..., "page": ..., "page_size": ..., "pages": ...}`, using the defaults described above for whichever of the new flags weren't given. `page` defaults to `1`; `page_size` defaults to `15` and cannot exceed `40`.

4. Update `README.md`: document the new flags, and add a short new section with these two example invocations and their exact output: `python cli.py list --tag ref --tag howto --any-tag` and `python cli.py list --page 2 --page-size 2`, both run against five bookmarks added in this order: `https://a.example.com/1` "Zebra Guide" tags `ref`+`howto`, `https://b.example.com/2` "Beta Tools" tag `howto`, `https://c.example.com/3` "Charlie Notes" tag `ref`, `https://d.example.com/4` "delta reference" tags `ref`+`extra`, and `https://e.example.com/5` "apple five" with no tags - none of them visited.

`stats` must keep reporting every bookmark and every visit regardless of anything passed to `list` - it has its own counts and should not be touched. `list`, `show`, and `stats` must stay read-only (no writes to the bookmark file), and every bookmark dict `list_bookmarks()` hands back must stay an independent copy, same as today. Keep `add`/`show`/`visit`/`delete` working exactly as they do now, including `add`'s existing merge-on-duplicate-url behavior (idempotent) and `visit`'s existing behavior of incrementing on every call (not idempotent).
